UK here. A friend of mine who works in HR once told me that there are only two UK universities that will automatically guarantee a job interview. Interestingly, they're not Oxford and Cambridge, but the Open University and Birkbeck College, London. The point is that these days anyone can get a degree, and this is no guarantee of competence, as standards of admission and teaching at some universities (basically the former polytechnics and teacher-training colleges) are now extremely low. I've had the misfortune of teaching "graduates" from such "universities" as Leeds Metropolitan (now Leeds Beckett), London Metropolitan and Sheffield Hallam, amongst others, and have been shocked by their poor intellectual calibre. However, a degree from the Open University or Birkbeck conveys a different and altogether more powerful message: that you value education, have a desire to learn and improve yourself that has required a real price to be paid in terms of personal time and money spent, and have the persistence and ability to manage your life that taking such a part-time degree requires. If you have a degree from one of those institutions it's easy to see what kind of person you are.

For myself, college seemed like "the time of my life" at the time, and I certainly had a lot of fun and went to a lot of parties, but with the benefit of hindsight I can see that most of this was not because I was at college, but because I was a particular age.
